brief.meaningEn: A familiar situation or range of activities in which someone feels secure and at ease.
brief.meaningZh: 某人感到安心自在的熟悉情況或活動範圍。
brief.grammar: in/within/outside/beyond one’s comfort zone; take/push someone out of their comfort zone; this noun frame can describe staying or moving beyond familiarity.
brief.register: Established psychological-space metaphor. Unfamiliarity can be challenging without proving inability; staying with a familiar task may also be a reasonable choice.
brief.boundaryZh: 超出熟悉範圍不代表實際危險，也不保證必成長；應按能力、支援及意願決定步幅，不貶低選擇暫留熟悉做法的人。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是道德測驗，不能因緊張便說不適合，也不能以此要求接受每項邀請。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用名詞搭配說明熟悉與陌生的範圍，提出合適嘗試。

sources.locatorNote: PDF page 129, table 1, row 2

listening.en: Editing the radio notes was within my comfort zone, but interviewing a guest was outside it; I agreed to ask one prepared question with the experienced host beside me, rather than lead the whole programme.
listening.zh: 整理電台筆記在我熟悉安心範圍內，但訪問嘉賓在範圍外；我答應在有經驗主持陪同下問一條預備問題，不是帶整個節目。
listening.promptZh: 哪項熟悉，怎樣嘗試陌生部分？

options.en: Editing felt familiar, and the speaker would try one interview question with support.
options.zh: 編筆記感熟悉，說話者會有支援地試一條訪問題。

options.en: Interviewing already felt easier than editing, so the speaker would lead the whole programme alone.
options.zh: 訪問已比編筆記輕鬆，所以說話者會獨帶全節目。

options.en: The speaker agreed to join the interview only after it had finished recording.
options.zh: 說話者在訪問錄完後才答應加入。

options.en: The speaker rejected all participation, including the editing work.
options.zh: 說話者拒絕全部參與，包括編輯工作。

listening.explanationZh: 熟悉編輯與初試訪問可並存；一題有支援是已答應的安排，不是獨管、錄後才加入或全拒。

reply.promptZh: 你打算怎樣嘗試第一次訪問？
reply.promptEn: How do you plan to try interviewing for the first time?

options.en: I will ask one prepared question with the experienced host beside me.
options.zh: 我會在有經驗主持旁問一條預備問題。

options.en: It is outside my comfort zone, so I will begin with one supported question rather than the whole programme.
options.zh: 它在我熟悉安心範圍外，所以先試一條有支援問題，而非全節目。

options.en: I have agreed to a small interview role while keeping the host’s guidance.
options.zh: 我答應小訪問角色，保留主持指導。

options.en: The first attempt will be prepared and limited in scope, not an entire solo programme.
options.zh: 首次嘗試會有預備且範圍有限，不是整個獨立節目。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都答一條預備問題及支援範圍，不把陌生當不能試或全盤承諾。

scene.promptZh: 畫家熟習鉛筆素描，但第一次試水彩，決定先畫一小片顏色練習，不立刻接大型委託。哪句準確？

options.en: Watercolour is beyond her comfort zone, so she is starting with a small colour study.
options.zh: 水彩在她熟悉安心範圍外，所以先做小色彩練習。

options.en: She already feels equally at ease with every watercolour commission as with pencil sketches.
options.zh: 她對每項水彩委託已跟鉛筆素描同樣自在。

options.en: The small study means she has accepted a large watercolour commission.
options.zh: 小練習表示她已接受大型水彩委託。

scene.explanationZh: 新媒介配小試行，不等於已同熟或已接大委託。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 outside someone’s comfort zone 推出？

options.en: The activity goes beyond what feels familiar and easy to that person.
options.zh: 活動超出當事人感熟悉自在之處。

options.en: The person is definitely incapable of learning it.
options.zh: 當事人肯定無法學會。

options.en: Preparation or a supported first step may help the person decide whether to try.
options.zh: 預備或有支援第一步可能幫決定是否試。

contrast.explanationZh: 不熟或不自在未證無法學，不以名詞當能力判決。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想因訪問超出你熟悉範圍，就報你不再適合做任何電台工作；你編筆記很熟，亦願試一題。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Keep the distinction between familiar editing and a new interview role, and describe the supported first step I agreed to.
options.zh: 分清熟悉編輯及新訪問角色，說明我答應的有支援第一步。

options.en: Remove me from both editing and interviewing without discussing the role I am ready to try.
options.zh: 不談我願試角色，便把編輯及訪問都取消。

options.en: Keep me on editing only and postpone the prepared question, although I have agreed to try it with the host.
options.zh: 即使我已答應跟主持試準備問題，仍只讓我編筆記，把問題延後。

dialogue.explanationZh: 分清熟悉工作及已願意試的部分，不全排除，也不忽略本人已答應的有支援嘗試。

speaking.en: This task is outside my comfort zone, but I would like to try a small part with clear support before taking on more.
speaking.zh: 任務在我熟悉安心範圍外，但我想先有清楚支援地試小部分，再接更多。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再以名詞搭配說熟悉範圍及嘗試步幅。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你本周已處理搬家，朋友又邀你周末參加新即興活動。你喜歡探索，但這次想選熟悉的安靜素描來休息，並謝邀請，不把留在熟悉範圍說成失敗或承諾下次一定來。用一至兩句英文回覆。

examples.en: Thank you for inviting me, but I want to stay within my comfort zone this weekend and spend a quiet afternoon sketching. After the move, familiar drawing feels like the rest I need, rather than a failure to be adventurous.
examples.zh: 謝謝邀請，但這周末我想留在熟悉安心範圍，安靜畫一下午；搬家後熟悉的畫畫是所需休息，不是缺乏探索心的失敗。

examples.en: I appreciate the invitation, though I am choosing my comfort zone this time because the week has been demanding. I would like some familiar sketching instead of another new activity just now.
examples.zh: 我感謝邀請，但這周忙碌，所以這次選熟悉安心範圍；我現在想做熟悉素描，不再加一項新活動。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以本周資源及休息需要選熟悉活動，禮貌回應邀請，不貶低自己或對下次作未定承諾。

takeaways.en: The new role took me beyond my comfort zone, so I asked what support would be available for the first session.
takeaways.zh: 新角色帶我超出熟悉安心範圍，所以我問首場有甚麼支援。

takeaways.en: Her comfort zone included familiar recipes, but she chose to try one new dish with her friend.
takeaways.zh: 她熟悉安心範圍包括熟悉食譜，但選跟朋友試一道新菜。

titleZh: 令人欣喜、耳目一新的改變

brief.meaningEn: A welcome, refreshing change from what someone has become used to.
brief.meaningZh: 相對原本習慣的情況，令人歡迎、精神一新的改變。
brief.grammar: someone/something is/was a breath of fresh air; say what changed and why it was welcome to the speaker.
brief.register: Established air metaphor. It expresses an evaluation, not proof that every new approach is better or everyone agrees.
brief.boundaryZh: 新本身不代表好，要有受歡迎的具體差異；不等於所有舊做法都應取消。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可保留說話者喜好來源，不把一人感受改成全體評分。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體正面差異描述令人欣喜的新氣象。

listening.en: After meetings full of announcements, the new chair’s opening question was a breath of fresh air for me: she asked which problem needed discussion and let members choose one before the notices.
listening.zh: 會議原本滿是宣布，新主席開場問題對我而言令人耳目一新；她問哪個問題需討論，讓成員先選一項，再讀通告。
listening.promptZh: 說話者歡迎哪個改變？

options.en: Members could choose a problem to discuss before hearing the notices.
options.zh: 成員可先選問題討論，再聽通告。

options.en: The chair read all the notices first and left the members’ chosen problem until the end.
options.zh: 主席先讀全部通告，把成員選的問題留到最後。

options.en: The chair chose the opening problem herself and asked members only to listen to her answer.
options.zh: 主席自己選開場問題，只請成員聽她回答。

options.en: The opening kept announcements as the only activity, with no member choice.
options.zh: 開場仍只宣布，沒有成員選擇。

listening.explanationZh: 新安排讓成員先選問題，再讀通告；不是主席代選、通告在先或沒有選擇。

reply.promptZh: 新主席的開場為甚麼讓你感到耳目一新？
reply.promptEn: Why did you find the new chair’s opening refreshing?

options.en: She let members choose a problem instead of starting only with announcements.
options.zh: 她讓成員選問題，不只以宣布開始。

options.en: It was a breath of fresh air because we had a real choice about what to discuss first.
options.zh: 我們可真正選先談甚麼，所以它令人耳目一新。

options.en: The opening made room for a concern members wanted to explore.
options.zh: 開場為成員想探討的顧慮留空間。

options.en: I welcomed the chance to discuss something before the usual notices.
options.zh: 我歡迎在平常通告前先討論的機會。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明說話者歡迎的具體參與差異。

scene.promptZh: 讀者覺得一本雜誌總像人人毫無困難，新專欄坦白寫初學者犯錯及修正，讓她覺得較有共鳴；未問其他讀者。哪句準確？

options.en: The honest beginner column was a breath of fresh air for her, though we do not know how other readers responded.
options.zh: 坦白初學者專欄對她而言令人耳目一新，但未知其他讀者回應。

options.en: A reader survey has already confirmed that this column is the magazine’s most popular feature.
options.zh: 讀者調查已確認這專欄是雜誌最受歡迎部分。

options.en: She preferred the older impression that nobody faced difficulty and found the new column unwelcome.
options.zh: 她較喜歡舊有人人無困難的印象，不歡迎新專欄。

scene.explanationZh: 可歸她正面共鳴，不擴至所有讀者，也不倒轉她喜好。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 a breath of fresh air 的比喻？

options.en: A welcome change gives someone new energy or relief.
options.zh: 受歡迎改變令人有新活力或鬆一口氣。

options.en: A change is new, but the speaker finds it less helpful and does not welcome it.
options.zh: 改變雖新，說話者覺更無用而不歡迎。

options.en: A person brings an approach that someone finds refreshing.
options.zh: 某人帶來說話者覺耳目一新的做法。

contrast.explanationZh: 新但不歡迎未合這個正面評價。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想把你一人喜歡新開場，寫成每位成員都認為舊會議沒價值；還沒收其他意見。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Say why I welcomed the change, and ask other members before making a claim about everyone.
options.zh: 說我為何歡迎改變，概括每人前先問其他成員。

options.en: Use my positive reaction as the group’s final assessment without asking anyone else.
options.zh: 不問其他人，把我的正面反應當全組最終評價。

options.en: Keep the next meeting announcement-only and collect reactions to the changed opening afterwards.
options.zh: 下次會議只讀通告，之後才收對改動開場的反應。

dialogue.explanationZh: 歸本人感受並問其他意見，不以一人代全體，也不必先取消參與機會再收反應。

speaking.en: The new approach was a breath of fresh air for me because it made room for questions I had not been able to ask.
speaking.zh: 新做法對我而言令人耳目一新，因它為我原本無法提出的問題留空間。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再給正面改變的具體理由。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友選一首帶輕快節奏的新曲，讓你們一直只排慢歌的合奏有新感覺。你想在訊息肯定這個選曲，也請保留一首熟悉慢歌作對照，而不聲稱所有觀眾必喜歡新曲。用一至兩句英文回覆朋友。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以不同節奏肯定朋友選曲，提保留慢曲作對照，不推所有觀眾喜好或把舊曲全無價值。

examples.en: The lively new piece is a breath of fresh air after so many slow songs, and I am glad you suggested it. Could we keep one familiar slower piece too, so the programme has a contrast?
examples.zh: 排了很多慢歌後，輕快新曲令人耳目一新，我很高興你提它；也留一首熟悉較慢曲，讓曲目有對照好嗎？

examples.en: Your choice feels like a breath of fresh air for our rehearsals because it brings a different rhythm. I would enjoy playing it alongside one of the slower pieces rather than replacing them all.
examples.zh: 你選曲給排練不同節奏，令我覺耳目一新；我想把它跟一首慢曲一起演，不是全取代慢曲。

takeaways.en: The guest’s honest account of her first failed draft was a breath of fresh air after a series of polished success stories.
takeaways.zh: 一連串完美成功故事後，嘉賓坦白講首份失敗草稿，令人耳目一新。

takeaways.en: A short open discussion was a breath of fresh air in a programme that had usually consisted only of speeches.
takeaways.zh: 原本通常只有演說的活動加入短開放討論，令人耳目一新。

brief.meaningEn: A continuing force or activity that drives an individual’s growth in ability or understanding.
brief.meaningZh: 持續推動個人在能力或理解上成長的力量或活動。
brief.grammar: X is/becomes the engine of personal development; specify the growth process supported, rather than a literal machine.
brief.register: Productive engine-as-driving-force metaphor applied to individual growth, not a technical name for a guaranteed training method.
brief.boundaryZh: 重要動力未等於唯一因素，也不保證任何次數練習都有效；需交代學習及改進怎發生。
brief.misconceptionZh: 忙碌或重複本身不證成長，要有可觀察的反思、技巧或理解變化。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體持續做法解釋個人成長，不誇大成果。

sources.sentence: Practice is the engine of personal development.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 34, table 1, row 6; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: For the apprentice editor, thoughtful feedback became the engine of personal development: comparing readers’ questions with her drafts helped her make explanations clearer, though she still asked for advice on complex interviews.
listening.zh: 對學徒編輯，仔細回饋成了個人成長動力；把讀者問題與草稿比較，幫她解釋更清楚，但複雜訪談仍會請教。
listening.promptZh: 回饋怎推動成長？

options.en: She used readers’ questions to improve explanations and still sought help where needed.
options.zh: 她用讀者問題改進解釋，需時仍求助。

options.en: She counted the number of comments without changing any explanation.
options.zh: 她只數評語，沒有改任何解釋。

options.en: She now handles complex interviews without asking for advice.
options.zh: 她現處理複雜訪談時不會請教。

options.en: She avoided comparing comments with the text because feedback was meant only to praise her.
options.zh: 她不比評語與文字，因回饋只用來稱讚。

listening.explanationZh: 比較問題及改清楚是具體過程，不是數量本身、全能或只求讚。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼她把回饋視為成長的重要動力？
reply.promptEn: Why did she see feedback as an important force in her growth?

options.en: It helped her identify explanations readers did not understand.
options.zh: 它幫她找讀者不懂的解釋。

options.en: It became the engine of personal development by guiding clearer revisions to her drafts.
options.zh: 它指引較清楚的草稿修改，成了個人成長動力。

options.en: She could connect the questions with changes she made in the text.
options.zh: 她可把問題連到文中改動。

options.en: The comments gave her a way to improve rather than only a score to collect.
options.zh: 評語給改進方法，不只收集分數。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以回饋到修改的作用解釋成長動力。

scene.promptZh: 學員聽同伴說自己常太快接話，便在討論中先重述對方意思再提問；幾周後，同伴說較能把話說完。哪句貼切？

options.en: Learning to listen before replying became the engine of personal development in his relationships.
options.zh: 學先聽再回應，成了他在人際方面的個人成長動力。

options.en: His progress came from replying sooner, leaving less time for the other person to finish.
options.zh: 他因回應更快、讓對方更少時間說完而進步。

options.en: The feedback concerned his written spelling, rather than how he took turns in conversation.
options.zh: 回饋關乎書面拼字，不是交談輪次。

scene.explanationZh: 先重述再問改變了聆聽習慣，同伴能說完是具體線索；不是搶快或拼字。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 the engine of personal development 推出？

options.en: A factor supports continuing individual growth.
options.zh: 一個因素支持持續個人成長。

options.en: That factor is the only possible cause of all improvement.
options.zh: 該因素是所有改進唯一可能成因。

options.en: The context can describe how ability or understanding changes.
options.zh: 情境可描述能力或理解怎變。

contrast.explanationZh: 動力比喻不確立唯一因果。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想把多收評語當成長成績，卻還沒看有否用於修改。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Ask which comments led to changes and what became clearer, rather than count feedback alone.
options.zh: 問哪些評語帶來改動、甚麼更清楚，不只數回饋。

options.en: Choose the learner with the largest pile of comments without looking at any revision.
options.zh: 不看任何修改，就選評語最多的學員。

options.en: Judge the improvement from how encouraging the comments sound, without comparing the revised explanations.
options.zh: 不比修改後解釋，只按評語聽來多鼓勵去判進步。

dialogue.explanationZh: 需看哪些回饋連到修改及理解變化，不只評語數量或鼓勵語氣。

speaking.en: Reflection can be the engine of personal development when I use what I notice to change my next attempt.
speaking.zh: 若把留意到的用於改下一次，反思可成為個人成長動力。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把成長動力連到可見的改變。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你申請加入跨代口述歷史小組，不只想替履歷加一行。你想解釋聽不同人生經驗可推動自己重新理解家庭，並願記下原有假設被改動的地方，不聲稱只參加便一定成熟。用一至兩句英文寫參加理由。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以聽跨代經驗及重想家庭假設說參加理由，提出記理解變化，不以履歷一行或參加本身代成長。

examples.en: Listening across generations could be the engine of personal development for me if I question my assumptions about family life. I would keep notes on what changes my understanding, rather than treat participation as just another line on a form.
examples.zh: 若我質疑對家庭生活的假設，聽跨代經驗可成為我的個人成長動力；我會記甚麼改了理解，不只把參與當表格多一行。

examples.en: I hope these conversations can become the engine of personal development by helping me see experiences beyond my own. I am ready to record which of my assumptions I need to reconsider.
examples.zh: 我盼對話幫看自己以外經驗，成為個人成長動力；我願記哪些原有假設需重新考慮。

takeaways.en: Honest questions became the engine of personal development when she began using them to rethink her first explanation.
takeaways.zh: 她開始用坦白問題重想首次解釋時，問題成了個人成長動力。

takeaways.en: For him, regular reflection was the engine of personal development, while a mentor helped him notice habits he had missed.
takeaways.zh: 對他而言，定期反思是個人成長動力，導師則幫他看到漏看的習慣。

brief.meaningEn: Increase the range of what someone knows about, has experienced or can imagine.
brief.meaningZh: 增加某人所知、體驗或能想像的範圍。
brief.grammar: widen/broaden/expand someone’s horizons; Cambridge lists these as one idiom. Plural horizons is usual for the range of someone’s knowledge, experience or imagined possibilities.
brief.register: Established spatial metaphor. Exposure creates opportunities for learning, not automatic expertise or a ranking of cultures.
brief.boundaryZh: 見得更多不表示完全懂或原有生活較差；需指出新增經驗及所學，而非只把移動等同成長。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可透過閱讀、交流或新角色開眼界，不必只限旅行，也不保證一次見聞消除偏見。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明新接觸如何增加理解，保留學習範圍。

listening.en: Helping at the community radio station widened my horizons because I heard residents explain jobs I had never considered; I began asking different questions, without claiming to understand every job after one recording.
listening.zh: 在社區電台幫忙開闊了我的眼界，因我聽居民解釋從未考慮的工作；我開始問不同問題，未聲稱一次錄製後就懂每種工作。
listening.promptZh: 開眼界的具體改變是甚麼？

options.en: New accounts of work led the speaker to ask questions beyond earlier experience.
options.zh: 新的工作敘述讓說話者問原有經驗以外的問題。

options.en: The speaker had already worked in the newly described jobs before joining the recording.
options.zh: 說話者加入錄製前，已做過新被介紹的工作。

options.en: The speaker heard only accounts of the same job they already knew well.
options.zh: 說話者只聽已熟悉的同一工作敘述。

options.en: The recording confirmed the speaker’s old questions without raising any different ones.
options.zh: 錄製確認說話者舊問題，沒有引出不同問題。

listening.explanationZh: 未想過的工作敘述引出新問題；不是先做過、只聽熟悉工作或原問法未變。

reply.promptZh: 社區電台經驗怎開闊你的眼界？
reply.promptEn: How did the community radio experience broaden what you knew?

options.en: I heard about jobs outside the range I had previously considered.
options.zh: 我聽到以往沒考慮的工作。

options.en: It widened my horizons by bringing residents’ unfamiliar working experiences into my questions.
options.zh: 它把居民陌生工作經驗帶進我的問題，開闊我的眼界。

options.en: I began asking about work I had not known how to imagine before.
options.zh: 我開始問以前不知怎想像的工作。

options.en: Those conversations gave me new subjects to explore rather than complete expertise.
options.zh: 那些對話給我新題目探究，不是完全專業知識。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都答新增工作理解及問題，不以接觸當已全懂。

scene.promptZh: 你一直只讀同一類結局，讀書會讓你看一篇沒有明確和解的故事，開始問留白作用；仍可喜歡原本類型。哪句貼切？

options.en: The discussion broadened my horizons by introducing a way of ending a story I had not considered.
options.zh: 討論讓我接觸未想過的結尾方法，開闊眼界。

options.en: The discussion settled which ending the writer must choose for the reader’s own unfinished story.
options.zh: 討論已決定讀者自己未完故事必須選哪種結尾。

options.en: The reader concluded that the ending clearly settled the disagreement, rather than leaving reconciliation open.
options.zh: 讀者斷定結尾已清楚解決爭執，而非讓和解保持未定。

scene.explanationZh: 接觸未想過結尾、開始問留白是擴範圍，未替自己的稿定結局，也不把未明確和解讀成已解決。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 widen someone’s horizons？

options.en: New experiences lead someone to consider ideas beyond what they knew.
options.zh: 新經驗令人考慮原本所知以外的想法。

options.en: Someone repeats a familiar activity without encountering or considering anything new.
options.zh: 某人只重複熟悉活動，沒接觸或考慮新事。

options.en: Reading accounts of unfamiliar lives changes the questions someone asks.
options.zh: 讀陌生人生記述改了某人所問問題。

contrast.explanationZh: 重複本身未顯示所知或經驗範圍擴大。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想把一次電台錄製寫成你已懂所有行業，但你只是開始問新問題。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Say which accounts opened new questions for me, while keeping clear that I am still learning about those jobs.
options.zh: 說哪些敘述給我新問題，同時說清我仍在學那些工作。

options.en: Describe the first recording as the final answer to the questions it has just raised.
options.zh: 把首次錄製寫成它剛引出問題的最終答案。

options.en: Keep only the familiar job in the account and omit the new work experiences that changed my questions.
options.zh: 敘述只留熟悉工作，略去改變我問題的新工作經驗。

dialogue.explanationZh: 需交代新接觸帶來哪些新問題，不把啟發當已答完，也不只留下原熟悉範圍。

speaking.en: I want to widen my horizons by listening to experiences outside my own, while being careful not to claim I understand everything at once.
speaking.zh: 我想聽自己以外經驗來開眼界，同時留意不聲稱立即全懂。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再指出新增經驗及學習範圍。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友想教你一種你從未玩的合作桌遊，你原本只玩輸贏各自計算的遊戲。你想欣然接受，說共同解題可讓你看到另一種互動，也請先用一輪示範規則，不說新遊戲必優於所有舊遊戲。用一至兩句英文回覆。
writing.selfCheckZh: 接受合作解題新體驗，請示範一輪了解共同決定，不把新舊遊戲作絕對排名或聲稱已懂規則。

examples.en: I would like to try it because a cooperative game could widen my horizons beyond the competitive games I know. Could you guide us through one round so I can see how the shared decisions work?
examples.zh: 我想試，因合作遊戲可在我所知競爭遊戲以外開眼界；可否帶一輪，讓我看共同決定怎運作？

examples.en: This could broaden my horizons by showing me a different way for players to solve a problem together. I would welcome a short demonstration before we begin, rather than assume the rules are the same as my usual games.
examples.zh: 這可展示玩家一起解問題的不同方法，開闊眼界；開始前我歡迎短示範，不假定規則跟平常遊戲一樣。

takeaways.en: The exchange broadened her horizons by giving her a chance to hear how another family organised its daily life.
takeaways.zh: 交流讓她有機會聽另一家庭怎安排日常，開闊眼界。

takeaways.en: Reading unfamiliar voices widened our horizons and left us with more questions to explore together.
takeaways.zh: 閱讀陌生聲音開闊我們眼界，也留下更多可一起探究的問題。

titleZh: 使生活或安排大幅改變

brief.meaningEn: Disrupt or radically change a familiar routine, life or arrangement.
brief.meaningZh: 打亂或大幅改變熟悉作息、生活或安排。
brief.grammar: turn a routine/life upside down; be turned upside down by + change; active/passive and possessive variants share the disruption/change sense.
brief.register: Established orientation metaphor, figurative here. A major change may be difficult, welcome or mixed, depending on context.
brief.boundaryZh: 大變動不等於永遠混亂、全部有害或所有部分都已改；需交代受影響安排。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可形容轉變而仍有穩定部分，不因強烈意象便編事故或失敗。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述大變動及具體適應，不把比喻當物理倒轉。

listening.en: The temporary move turned our routine upside down: the bus came earlier, dinner was later and the shared room had to serve as a study space, though we kept our Sunday call with Grandad.
listening.zh: 臨時搬遷打亂作息：巴士較早、晚飯較晚，共用房間要兼溫習空間，但仍保留周日跟祖父通話。
listening.promptZh: 大變動與保留的是甚麼？

options.en: Transport, meals and room use changed, while the Sunday call continued.
options.zh: 交通、用餐及房間用途改了，周日通話仍繼續。

options.en: Every family routine stopped, including the Sunday call.
options.zh: 所有家庭作息都停了，包括周日通話。

options.en: Meals and transport stayed as before; only the Sunday call changed.
options.zh: 用餐及交通都照舊，只有周日通話改了。

options.en: The family had already returned to its old home before the bus time changed.
options.zh: 巴士時間改前，家庭已搬回舊居。

listening.explanationZh: 多項日常改動支持意象，仍保留一項，不是所有都停，也不是只有通話改。

reply.promptZh: 臨時搬遷怎影響你們日常？
reply.promptEn: How did the temporary move affect daily life?

options.en: We had earlier transport, later meals and a shared room that also became a study space.
options.zh: 交通較早、吃飯較晚，共用房也兼溫習。

options.en: It turned our routine upside down, although we still kept the Sunday call.
options.zh: 它打亂我們作息，雖仍保留周日通話。

options.en: Several familiar arrangements changed at once, rather than just one small detail.
options.zh: 多項熟悉安排同時改，不只一個小細節。

options.en: The family needed to adapt its timings and room use while keeping one regular contact.
options.zh: 家庭需適應時間及房間用途，也保留一項定期聯絡。

reply.explanationZh: 四句答多項日常變動並保留範圍，不加永久結果。

scene.promptZh: 舞台換裝修後，排練地、器材存放及演出時間都需重排，但演員名單沒變。哪句準確？

options.en: The renovation turned the rehearsal arrangements upside down without changing the cast.
options.zh: 裝修改亂排練安排，沒有改演員名單。

options.en: Rehearsals can still use the same room and equipment positions, with only a change to the starting time.
options.zh: 排練仍可用同一房間及器材位置，只改開始時間。

options.en: The cast was replaced before anyone discussed the room or equipment.
options.zh: 討論房間或器材前，演員已被替換。

scene.explanationZh: 場地存放時間都需重排，不只是開始時間改，名單仍保留。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 turned upside down 的本課比喻推出？

options.en: Familiar arrangements changed substantially.
options.zh: 熟悉安排大幅改變。

options.en: Nothing stable can remain and the change must be permanently harmful.
options.zh: 不能有任何穩定部分，改變必永久有害。

options.en: The context can show which parts of life were disrupted.
options.zh: 情境可示生活哪些部分被打亂。

contrast.explanationZh: 意象強不決定所有部分或永久好壞。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想因作息大變，就把你們寫成斷了所有家人聯絡，但周日通話仍在。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Describe the changed timings and room use, but keep the continuing Sunday call in the account.
options.zh: 描述時間及房間用途改動，但保留持續周日通話。

options.en: Use the move as a reason to stop the Sunday call without asking anyone whether the time still works.
options.zh: 不問時間仍否可行，便以搬遷為由停周日通話。

options.en: Mention only the call and leave out the changes that required the family to adapt.
options.zh: 只提通話，刪家庭需適應的改動。

dialogue.explanationZh: 大變與保留可並存，不需自行停聯絡或只選穩定而抹改變。

speaking.en: The change turned our routine upside down, so we are deciding which familiar parts we can keep while adjusting the rest.
speaking.zh: 改變打亂作息，所以我們正決定哪些熟悉部分可保留、其餘怎調。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說大變動及仍保留的部分。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫故事作者後記，角色本來把自己當不會教人的安靜人，一次被請代帶小組，改了他對自己的想法，開始願意練講解；家庭作息並沒改。你想用這意象說明自我看法大變，保留他仍需練習，不說一次便變完美老師。用一至兩句英文寫後記。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以自我看法及願學轉變說大改，分清家庭作息未動，不以一次經驗保證教學專業或人物轉變全成。

examples.en: Leading the small group turned his view of himself upside down: he began to imagine teaching as something he could learn. I would keep his need for practice rather than make one session turn him into an expert.
examples.zh: 帶小組大改他對自己的看法，讓他開始想像教學是可學的事；我會保留練習需要，不用一次變專家。

examples.en: His idea of who he could become was turned upside down by the unexpected teaching role. The ending shows a willingness to practise, not a completely finished transformation.
examples.zh: 意外教學角色大改他對能成為怎樣的人的想法；結尾展示願意練，不是轉變已全完成。

takeaways.en: The new role turned her usual working day upside down, but she kept one quiet hour for planning.
takeaways.zh: 新角色大改她平常工作日，但她保留一小時安靜規劃。

takeaways.en: Their plans were turned upside down by the unexpected closure, and they began looking for a workable alternative.
takeaways.zh: 意外關閉打亂他們計劃，他們開始找可行替代。

brief.meaningEn: Examine or discuss the parts of something carefully, often one after another.
brief.meaningZh: 仔細看過或討論某事的各部分，常按次序逐項進行。
brief.grammar: go through + instructions/list/scene with someone; went/gone/going; focus here is examination/discussion, while go through a difficult experience is another established sense.
brief.register: Common phrasal verb with multiple established senses. In these examination contexts, explain what is reviewed and what follow-up remains; experiencing difficulty is a different use.
brief.boundaryZh: 逐項看不表示每項都已解決或核為真，也不必只讀不問；需交代檢視目的及待處理。
brief.misconceptionZh: 過了一遍流程與完成所有改動不同，能找問題仍可有工作未完。
brief.outcomeZh: 能請求或描述逐項檢視，分清檢視與完成修正。

listening.en: We went through the visitor instructions together, stopping at the entrance step because two signs used different names; the review found the mismatch, but the signs still needed changing.
listening.zh: 我們一起逐項看訪客指示，在入口步驟停下，因兩標示用不同名字；檢視找出不符，但標示仍需改。
listening.promptZh: 已做及未做的是甚麼？

options.en: The team reviewed the steps and identified a mismatch, while changing the signs remained.
options.zh: 團隊檢視步驟並找出不符，改標示仍未做。

options.en: The signs had already been replaced before anyone read the instructions.
options.zh: 讀指示前，標示已替換。

options.en: The team only experienced an unpleasant event and did not examine any text.
options.zh: 團隊只經歷不愉快事件，沒檢視文字。

options.en: Both signs were confirmed to use the same entrance name throughout the review.
options.zh: 整次檢視確認兩標示用同一入口名。

listening.explanationZh: go through此處逐項檢視，找到差異但未改，不是經歷義或已一致。

reply.promptZh: 一起看訪客指示時，你們發現甚麼？
reply.promptEn: What did you discover when you reviewed the visitor instructions together?

options.en: The entrance step used names that did not match across the two signs.
options.zh: 入口步驟的兩標示名字不符。

options.en: We went through the steps and found a mismatch at the entrance.
options.zh: 我們逐項看步驟，發現入口有不符。

options.en: Comparing the instructions with the signs showed where visitors could be confused.
options.zh: 比較指示及標示，看到訪客可能混亂之處。

options.en: The review identified a change needed in the signs, rather than completing it.
options.zh: 檢視找出標示需改，而非已完成改動。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都答檢視發現的名字差異及待改，不把review當已修。

scene.promptZh: 你們用清單逐個談活動角色，發現缺一個迎新負責人，現想問誰願接，還沒分配。哪句貼切？

options.en: We have gone through the roles and found a welcome task that still needs someone.
options.zh: 我們已逐項看角色，找到仍需人負責的迎新任務。

options.en: Every role was already assigned before the list was discussed.
options.zh: 談清單前，每個角色已分配。

options.en: The team avoided discussing the role list and only waited for the event to begin.
options.zh: 團隊避談角色清單，只等活動開始。

scene.explanationZh: 逐項談找出缺人，不等於全分配或沒檢視。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不是本課 go through 的仔細檢視意思？

options.en: Review the stages of a plan together and raise questions.
options.zh: 一起檢視計劃階段並提問。

options.en: Experience a difficult year without discussing or examining a list or process.
options.zh: 經歷難過一年，並非討論或檢視清單流程。

options.en: Discuss each part of a scene to clarify what happens.
options.zh: 談場景各部分以釐清發生甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: 經歷困難是另一常用義，此課聚焦檢視討論；不要只看同詞便混義。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說大家已看過指示，就可不用改已找出的兩個入口名；你想處理發現。哪個回應最好？

options.en: The review showed what needs changing; let us agree who will make the entrance names consistent.
options.zh: 檢視顯示需改甚麼；一起議誰把入口名改一致。

options.en: Run the same visitor trial again before making any plan to address the known name mismatch.
options.zh: 未計劃處理已知名字不符，先重跑同樣訪客試行。

options.en: Archive the review notes and leave the entrance signs as they are for the next event.
options.zh: 把檢視筆記歸檔，下次活動入口標示照舊。

dialogue.explanationZh: 檢視是找需改部分，應有具體負責改動，不只重試或歸檔。

speaking.en: Could we go through the scene together and pause where the character’s intention is unclear?
speaking.zh: 可否一起逐項看場景，在角色意圖不清的地方停一停？
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再提出檢視範圍及目的。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你學朗讀家書，覺得一段很快便讀完，卻不知道哪些停頓可讓聽者明白情緒。你想請有經驗朋友一起看那一段，每到語氣改變便停下討論，再試讀，不只是請他說好不好。用一至兩句英文提出練習請求。
writing.selfCheckZh: 請逐段談語氣及試停頓，提出聆聽回饋目的，不把看過便當表達已熟或所有問題已解。

examples.en: Could we go through this passage together and stop where the tone changes? I want to try the pauses aloud and hear whether they help the listener follow the feeling.
examples.zh: 可否一起逐項看這段，在語氣改變處停下？我想大聲試停頓，聽是否幫聽者跟上情緒。

examples.en: I would like to go through the letter with you, discussing one change of tone at a time. Could you listen as I try the pauses, rather than give only an overall judgement?
examples.zh: 我想跟你逐項看信，每次談一個語氣變化；我試停頓時，可否聽一下，不只給整體評價？

takeaways.en: We went through the plan with the new volunteer and marked two questions to discuss before the event.
takeaways.zh: 我們跟新義工逐項看計劃，標了活動前需談的兩個問題。

takeaways.en: The tutor is going through the dialogue with us, pausing to ask what each speaker is trying to achieve.
takeaways.zh: 導師正跟我們逐項看對話，停下問每位說話者想達到甚麼。

brief.meaningEn: Accept new positions or responsibilities and the work associated with them.
brief.meaningZh: 接受新位置或職責，連同相關工作。
brief.grammar: take on new roles/a new role; took/has taken on; take on + responsibility is the accept-duty sense, not acquire an appearance or compete against someone.

brief.boundaryZh: 承接角色不等於立即精通、做全部工作或不能協商；需分清邀請、同意及實際履行。
brief.misconceptionZh: 問清工作量是負責任考慮，不應把有意了解當已承諾。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明新職責、同意範圍及需要的支援。

listening.en: Two members took on new roles in the reading group: one welcomed first-time visitors and the other gathered questions, while the tutor continued to choose the texts with the whole group.
listening.zh: 讀書會兩成員承接新角色：一位接待首次訪客，另一位收問題，導師仍跟全組一起選文章。
listening.promptZh: 新的責任怎樣分配？

options.en: The two members handled welcoming and question collection, while text choice remained shared with the tutor.
options.zh: 兩成員負責接待及收問題，選文仍與導師共同處理。

options.en: The two members took over choosing the texts, while the tutor handled only welcoming.
options.zh: 兩成員接管選文，導師只管接待。

options.en: The members were only considering the invitation and had not accepted any duties.
options.zh: 成員只考慮邀請，未接任何職責。

options.en: Both members continued their original work without any change in responsibility.
options.zh: 兩成員繼續原工作，責任沒有改變。

listening.explanationZh: took on表示已接兩項職責，選文仍共同，不是只邀請、無改動或取代導師。

reply.promptZh: 兩位成員在讀書會承接了甚麼？
reply.promptEn: What did the two members take responsibility for in the reading group?

options.en: One welcomed new visitors and the other collected questions.
options.zh: 一位接待新訪客，另一位收問題。

options.en: They took on new roles in welcoming visitors and gathering questions.
options.zh: 他們承接了接待訪客及收問題的新角色。

options.en: They accepted two practical responsibilities without taking over the shared choice of texts.
options.zh: 他們接兩項實務責任，沒取代共同選文。

options.en: Their duties expanded to the arrival and question stages of the session.
options.zh: 他們職責擴至活動接待及問題環節。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都給所接職責，不把角色擴展作全盤管理。

scene.promptZh: 編輯邀你下期聯絡投稿人，你回覆想先知需花多久，還未同意。哪句準確？

options.en: I have been invited to take on a new role, but I am still asking about the time it would require.
options.zh: 我獲邀接新角色，但仍在問所需時間。

options.en: I have accepted the role and already contacted the contributors.
options.zh: 我已接角色，並已聯絡投稿人。

options.en: The invitation asks me to redesign the cover rather than contact writers.
options.zh: 邀請要我重設封面，而非聯絡作者。

scene.explanationZh: 邀請加問時間不等於已接或已做，亦不是另一任務。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以證明 someone has taken on a new role？

options.en: They have agreed to handle a responsibility that was not theirs before.
options.zh: 他們已同意處理原本不屬自己的責任。

options.en: They have received an invitation and are still deciding whether the duties fit.
options.zh: 他們收到邀請，仍決定職責是否合適。

options.en: They begin the new duty after agreeing its scope with the group.
options.zh: 與小組議定範圍後開始新職責。

contrast.explanationZh: 收到邀請及考慮不等於已承接。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想因兩人接了新角色，就把所有選文也交他們，不再問全組；原安排仍共同選。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Keep their agreed duties clear and discuss any further responsibility with them and the group first.
options.zh: 說清已議職責，再加責任前先跟他們及全組談。

options.en: Add text selection to their duties now and inform the group after the next session.
options.zh: 現加選文職責，下次活動後才通知全組。

options.en: Remove the new welcoming and question roles because text choice remains shared.
options.zh: 因選文仍共同，就取消新接待及收問題角色。

dialogue.explanationZh: 新角色有範圍，不自動加未議職責，也不因仍有共同決策便取消分工。

speaking.en: I am willing to take on a new role if we agree on the duties, the time involved and where I can ask for help.
speaking.zh: 若議定職責、所需時間及求助地方，我願接新角色。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說承接職責的範圍及條件。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你在實習反思寫自己原來只整理資料，今次第一次主持五分鐘的訪問開場，問完預備題便交回導師。你想記錄已承接的小角色及一項要改善的地方，不把這次寫成已能獨立做全訪問。用一至兩句英文反思。
writing.selfCheckZh: 描述已做五分鐘開場及交回導師的範圍，選停頓回應時間作改善，不自稱已獨管全訪問。

examples.en: I took on a new role by leading the five-minute opening before handing the interview back to my tutor. Next time I want to leave a clearer pause after my prepared question.
examples.zh: 我主持五分鐘開場後把訪問交回導師，承接了新角色；下次想在預備問題後留較清楚停頓。

examples.en: Taking on a new role meant asking the opening question myself, not managing the whole interview alone. I would like to improve how I give the speaker time to answer before the handover.
examples.zh: 承接新角色是自己問開場題，不是獨管全訪問；我想改善交接前怎給講者時間答。

takeaways.en: They are considering whether to take on new roles, so they asked about the support and time involved.
takeaways.zh: 他們正考慮是否接新角色，所以問支援及所需時間。

brief.meaningEn: A feeling of reassurance or freedom from worry about a concern.
brief.meaningZh: 對一項顧慮感到放心，較少擔心的感覺。
brief.grammar: give/bring/provide someone peace of mind; for peace of mind; an uncountable feeling, distinct from proof that nothing can go wrong.
brief.register: Established phrase for reassurance. The source of reassurance should be clear and may address only part of a situation.
brief.boundaryZh: 安心不保證零風險、工作全完成或所有人同感；可放心一項而仍需處理另一項。
brief.misconceptionZh: 資訊清楚可帶來安心，不能把感受直接當客觀結果或服務已交付。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體依據表達放心，保留實際限制。

listening.en: Knowing who would collect the borrowed display gave me peace of mind, because I no longer had to guess whom to contact; the collection itself was still scheduled for tomorrow.
listening.zh: 知道誰會取回借來展示品讓我安心，因不再需猜聯絡誰；實際取回仍排明天。
listening.promptZh: 安心來自甚麼，未發生的是甚麼？

options.en: The contact responsibility is clear, while collection is still planned for tomorrow.
options.zh: 聯絡責任清楚，但取回仍計劃明天。

options.en: The display has already been collected and returned to its owner.
options.zh: 展示品已取回並還物主。

options.en: The speaker is reassured because the collection was cancelled without a new plan.
options.zh: 取回取消且沒新計劃，所以說話者放心。

options.en: The contact person remains unknown, but the speaker has stopped trying to find out.
options.zh: 聯絡人仍未知，但說話者已不再找。

listening.explanationZh: 知道負責人解聯絡顧慮，未等於取回完成或已取消。

reply.promptZh: 知道負責取回的人，為甚麼令你放心？
reply.promptEn: Why does knowing who will collect the display reassure you?

options.en: I now know whom to contact about the collection.
options.zh: 我現在知道取回事宜可聯絡誰。

options.en: It gives me peace of mind because I do not have to guess who is responsible.
options.zh: 它讓我安心，因不需猜誰負責。

options.en: One uncertainty about the handover has been cleared up.
options.zh: 交接的一項未知已釐清。

options.en: The arrangement has a named contact even though the pickup is tomorrow.
options.zh: 雖明天才取，安排已有具名聯絡人。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都給負責人清楚的安心依據，不把明天安排當已完成。

scene.promptZh: 你擔心讀稿會找不到入口，朋友寄一張清楚地圖及聯絡方法，讓你較放心，但還未出發。哪句準確？

options.en: The clear directions give me peace of mind before I travel, although I have not arrived yet.
options.zh: 清楚指引讓我出發前安心，雖尚未到達。

options.en: The directions confirm that I have already reached the correct room.
options.zh: 指引確認我已到正確房間。

options.en: The map gives me less information about the entrance than I had before.
options.zh: 地圖給我的入口資訊比原本少。

scene.explanationZh: 指引減出發顧慮，不是已抵達或資訊較少。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 peace of mind 推出？

options.en: A person feels reassured about a concern.
options.zh: 一個人對顧慮感到放心。

options.en: Every possible problem has been ruled out objectively.
options.zh: 每個可能問題都已客觀排除。

options.en: The context can explain what made the person less worried.
options.zh: 情境可解釋甚麼令較少擔心。

contrast.explanationZh: 感受放心不等於所有風險已排。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想因你已安心，就刪掉明天取回的提醒；取回仍未做。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Keep the reminder: knowing the contact reassures me, but the collection still needs to happen.
options.zh: 留提醒：知道聯絡人讓我放心，但取回仍需做。

options.en: Remove tomorrow’s reminder and check the collection only if the owner asks later.
options.zh: 刪明天提醒，物主之後問才查取回。

options.en: Arrange a different collector without telling the named contact, since the plan already feels settled.
options.zh: 既計劃感覺已定，不通知具名聯絡人就安排另一位取物。

dialogue.explanationZh: 安心與後續工作分清，保留提醒及已議交接，不等問才做或另改不告知。

speaking.en: The clear arrangement gives me peace of mind, while I still need to complete my part at the agreed time.
speaking.zh: 清楚安排讓我安心，同時我仍需在已議時間做自己部分。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清放心感受及仍需履行。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你把未公開故事草稿給朋友試讀，原擔心被轉寄。朋友答應只自己讀、周末回短評，你想道謝說這個清楚約定令你較安心，也願若他想引一段先問你，不以安心表示作品已完稿。用一至兩句英文回覆。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以私讀及不轉寄的清楚約定道謝，仍保留引用先問，勿把放心當已獲評語或故事完稿。

examples.en: Knowing you will read it privately gives me peace of mind, and I appreciate the clear plan for a short response at the weekend. Please ask before quoting any part of the draft elsewhere.
examples.zh: 知道你會私下讀讓我安心，我感謝周末回短評的清楚安排；在別處引草稿任何部分前，請先問。

examples.en: Your agreement not to forward the draft brings me peace of mind while I wait for your comments. I am happy to discuss a quotation if you ask me first.
examples.zh: 你答應不轉寄草稿，讓我等評語時安心；若先問，我樂意討論引用。

brief.meaningEn: Worry a great deal about minor matters, often in advice not to give them excessive attention.
brief.meaningZh: 為細小事情很擔心，常用來勸別給太多注意。
brief.grammar: do not/don’t sweat the small stuff; sweating the small stuff; decide what counts as minor in the actual situation.
brief.register: Informal sweat-as-worry idiom. What feels minor to one person may matter to another; do not use it to dismiss genuine needs or responsibilities.
brief.boundaryZh: 小不小需看後果，不是所有細節都可省；姓名、接達或關鍵時間看來細仍可能重要。
brief.misconceptionZh: 避免小題大作不等於無視所有問題，可按目的及影響排序。
brief.outcomeZh: 能區分不影響目的的小瑕疵及需處理的關鍵細節。

listening.en: Before our informal reading, I was sweating the small stuff over two slightly different paper shades, although everyone could read the same clear text; my partner suggested checking the missing page instead.
listening.zh: 非正式讀稿前，我為兩種稍不同紙色過分掛心，雖人人讀得到同樣清楚文字；伙伴建議改先查漏掉的一頁。
listening.promptZh: 哪項是小掛慮，哪項需先查？

options.en: The slight paper-shade difference mattered less than the missing page.
options.zh: 紙色小差異比漏頁沒那麼重要。

options.en: The missing page was already found, so only the paper colour remained.
options.zh: 漏頁已找到，所以只剩紙色。

options.en: The two colours made the text unreadable to the whole group.
options.zh: 兩紙色令全組讀不到文字。

options.en: The partner wanted to ignore the page and compare more shades first.
options.zh: 伙伴想不理漏頁，先再比紙色。

listening.explanationZh: 文字同樣清楚而只紙色略異，漏頁關內容；不是已補或伙伴先看色。

reply.promptZh: 伙伴為甚麼建議先查漏頁？
reply.promptEn: Why did your partner suggest checking the missing page first?

options.en: The missing page affects the reading more directly than the slight paper-shade difference.
options.zh: 漏頁比紙色略異更直接影響讀稿。

options.en: I was sweating the small stuff over the paper, while a page we needed was missing.
options.zh: 我們需的一頁漏掉時，我卻為紙的小事掛心。

options.en: The text was readable on both papers, but the group still needed the absent page.
options.zh: 兩種紙上文字都可讀，但小組仍需缺頁。

options.en: The next useful step was to restore the complete text rather than keep comparing shades.
options.zh: 有用下一步是補全文，不是繼續比色。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以完整內容優先說明，不以小事名義跳漏頁。

scene.promptZh: 朋友說姓名拼錯只是小事不必理，但這會讓來賓找不到自己的入場登記；你想指出影響。哪句最好？

options.en: Correcting the name is not just sweating the small stuff; it affects whether the guest can find the booking.
options.zh: 改姓名不只是為小事掛心；它影響來賓能否找登記。

options.en: The spelling can wait until after entry because the guest’s name is unrelated to finding the booking.
options.zh: 姓名與找登記無關，所以拼寫可等入場後。

options.en: The guest has already found the correct booking and asked us to leave the name unchanged.
options.zh: 來賓已找到正確登記，並請保留名字原樣。

scene.explanationZh: 姓名細節有實際入場影響，不能只因看來小便當無關；未說已解。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個理解最不符合 don’t sweat the small stuff？

options.en: Do not let minor issues take excessive attention away from the main purpose.
options.zh: 不要讓小事過度佔注意而離主要目的。

options.en: Ignore a detail even when it creates a clear barrier to participation.
options.zh: 即使細節造成清楚參與障礙，也不理。

options.en: Check whether a supposedly small issue has a practical consequence.
options.zh: 查所謂小事有否實際後果。

contrast.explanationZh: 不是叫忽略真實障礙，需按影響辨小事。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想因不要小題大作，就不補漏頁；那頁含最後一段要讀的內容。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Let the paper shade go, but replace the missing page so the reading has its complete text.
options.zh: 紙色可放下，但補缺頁，讓讀稿有完整文字。

options.en: Keep comparing paper shades and leave the absent passage for readers to infer.
options.zh: 繼續比紙色，缺段讓讀者自己推。

options.en: Remove the last passage from the plan without checking whether the group still wants to read it.
options.zh: 不問小組是否仍想讀最後段，就從計劃移除。

dialogue.explanationZh: 放下無關紙色不等於放內容；應補缺頁，不需未問便刪或留人猜。

speaking.en: I do not want to sweat the small stuff, but I will check whether a detail affects someone’s ability to take part.
speaking.zh: 我不想為小事過分掛心，但會查細節是否影響某人參與。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再按實際影響判斷小事。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你給第一次送出詩作的自己寫便條，總擔心寄稿信每行是否剛好同長，詩本身及收件地址已核，截止今晚。你想提醒自己別再為排版小差異掛心，按已核方式送出，不把回覆結果寫成保證。用一至兩句英文自我提醒。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出已核關鍵資料及不影響目的的行長間距，提醒按時寄出，不用小事說法跳實際未核項或保證獲選。

examples.en: I should not sweat the small stuff about equal line lengths in the covering note when the poem and address are already checked. I will send it tonight and accept that the editor’s response is still uncertain.
examples.zh: 詩及地址已核，不應再為寄稿便條每行同長的小事掛心；我今晚寄出，接受編輯回應仍未知。

examples.en: Instead of sweating the small stuff over the note’s spacing, I can use the checked submission details and send the poem before the deadline. A neat message does not need perfectly matching lines.
examples.zh: 不再為便條間距的小事掛心，我可按核過投稿資訊在期限前寄詩；整齊訊息不需每行完全一樣。

takeaways.en: She stopped sweating the small stuff over the folder colour and checked that the pages were in order.
takeaways.zh: 她不再為文件夾顏色小事掛心，改查頁次是否整齊。

takeaways.en: Do not sweat the small stuff about a slightly uneven heading when the group can read it and the main question is ready.
takeaways.zh: 標題稍不整齊但全組讀得到、主要問題也備好時，不必為這小事過分掛心。

titleZh: 由內在開始，帶來外在改變

brief.meaningEn: Beginning with internal qualities or understanding and extending to outward behaviour or expression.
brief.meaningZh: 從內在特質或理解開始，延伸到外在行為或表達。
brief.grammar: change/develop something from the inside out; this figurative direction differs from knowing something inside out, meaning thoroughly.
brief.register: Conventional directional image. State what inner change and outward effect the account actually shows; not a technical guarantee of transformation.
brief.boundaryZh: 由內到外不表示外觀全變或一次改永久，需具體連內在理解與表現；不拿衣服翻面混同本課。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要只換外觀便稱內在已變，也不以強烈比喻省去過程。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述內在變化如何表現在具體行動。

listening.en: The discussion changed her approach from the inside out: once she understood why the visitor felt excluded, she stopped reciting the same welcome and began asking what help the person wanted.
listening.zh: 討論由內到外改變她的做法；理解訪客為何感被排除後，她不再只背同樣歡迎詞，開始問對方想甚麼幫助。
listening.promptZh: 內在理解怎表現在行動？

options.en: Understanding the visitor’s experience led her to ask about wanted help rather than repeat a script.
options.zh: 理解訪客經驗讓她問所需幫助，不只背稿。

options.en: She changed the welcome sign but kept her understanding and questions exactly the same.
options.zh: 她換歡迎標示，理解及問題則完全不變。

options.en: She decided to ask colleagues to choose help for visitors, rather than ask the visitors themselves.
options.zh: 她決定讓同事替訪客選幫助，不問訪客本人。

options.en: The discussion concerned only the physical arrangement of the welcome desk.
options.zh: 討論只關迎新枱實際擺法。

listening.explanationZh: 理解被排除感帶動詢問，是內到外，不是只改標示、由同事代選或只談桌位。

reply.promptZh: 討論怎改了她的迎接方式？
reply.promptEn: How did the discussion change the way she welcomed visitors?

options.en: She understood the exclusion concern and began asking what help the visitor wanted.
options.zh: 她理解被排除的顧慮，開始問訪客想何幫助。

options.en: It changed her approach from the inside out, connecting understanding with a different welcome.
options.zh: 它把理解連到不同迎接方法，由內到外改變她做法。

options.en: Her new questions followed a change in how she saw the visitor’s experience.
options.zh: 新問題來自對訪客經驗看法改變。

options.en: She moved from repeating a script to responding to the person’s preferences.
options.zh: 她從只重複稿，轉向回應對方偏好。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都連內在理解與外在詢問，不只外觀。

scene.promptZh: 人物原本以為求助是軟弱，後來理解合作能補各自不足，開始在卡住時主動問同伴，而非只換衣着顯自信。哪句貼切？

options.en: His attitude is changing from the inside out, as a new view of cooperation leads him to ask for help.
options.zh: 新合作看法令他主動求助，他的態度正由內到外改變。

options.en: He has only changed his clothes, without rethinking help or acting differently.
options.zh: 他只換衣服，沒有重想幫助或不同行動。

options.en: He is describing detailed knowledge of the project, rather than a changed attitude towards asking for help.
options.zh: 他在描述對項目的詳細了解，而非對求助態度改變。

scene.explanationZh: 重想求助及開始行動是所給過程；knowinsideout是不同結構，不是此方向比喻。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 from the inside out 的本課意思？

options.en: A change in understanding affects how someone responds.
options.zh: 理解變化影響某人怎回應。

options.en: Only the outward display changes, with no described inner shift.
options.zh: 只改外在展示，沒描述內在轉變。

options.en: A person rethinks a belief and starts acting on the new view.
options.zh: 某人重想信念，開始按新觀點行動。

contrast.explanationZh: 只改外觀不足以證明內到外的過程。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想因新歡迎標示漂亮，就寫她已由內改變；其實她仍只背稿，未問訪客需要。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Describe the sign change accurately, and look for evidence of changed understanding or responses before claiming an inner shift.
options.zh: 準確描述標示改動，聲稱內在轉變前先看理解或回應有否改的證據。

options.en: Use the new sign alone as evidence that her view of visitors has changed.
options.zh: 只用新標示作她對訪客看法已改的證據。

options.en: Replace the questions about visitors’ experience with another redesign of the desk.
options.zh: 以再重設桌子取代詢問訪客經驗的問題。

dialogue.explanationZh: 外觀變不自證內在，需看理解及互動，不以再換外觀替代。

speaking.en: The experience changed my approach from the inside out when a different understanding led me to ask different questions.
speaking.zh: 不同理解令我問不同問題時，那經驗由內到外改變我的做法。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再連內在理解與外在反應。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你評一個演員演角色的片段，前版只用大聲表示憤怒，這次演員先理解角色怕失去朋友，於是用停頓、避開目光再試說真話。你想指出內在理解怎帶動表達，而不把安靜本身當更好的演法。用一至兩句英文給回饋。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出怕失朋友的理解與停頓目光等表達關係，不單以音量低高判演得較好或聲稱角色問題已解。

examples.en: Your performance changed from the inside out when you understood the character’s fear of losing a friend. The pauses and averted gaze now seem connected to what the character wants, not just a quieter voice.
examples.zh: 你理解角色怕失朋友後，演出由內到外改變；停頓及避開目光現連到角色所想，不只聲音較低。

examples.en: Working from the inside out helped you find a reason for the pause before the truth is spoken. I would keep exploring that fear rather than treat lower volume as the whole change.
examples.zh: 由內到外工作幫你找到說真話前停頓的理由；我會繼續探那恐懼，不把低音量當全部改變。

takeaways.en: The new understanding changed the project from the inside out, shaping both the questions we asked and the way we presented the answers.
takeaways.zh: 新理解由內到外改變項目，影響所問問題及呈現答案方式。

takeaways.en: She wanted to revise the character from the inside out, beginning with the belief behind his choices.
takeaways.zh: 她想由內到外修改角色，先從選擇背後信念開始。

notes: Distinct from1606 know something inside out (thorough familiarity), whose canonical already notes this direction-of-change sense boundary. Same words do not warrant a sense merge.

brief.meaningEn: In someone’s basic nature or deepest interests, even if outward roles suggest something else.
brief.meaningZh: 在某人基本性情或內心真正興趣上，即使外在角色看來不同。
brief.grammar: be an artist/a teacher/curious at heart; describe a supported character judgement rather than a literal location.
brief.register: Established inward-nature phrase. It can express someone’s self-description or an observer’s interpretation; it does not override what the person actually says or does.
brief.boundaryZh: 內在傾向不等於正式資格或全時職業，也不使所有行動必符合一個標籤；需有經驗線索及判斷來源。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能以自稱或他人一句話代所有行為證據，也不要替不認同的人強加身分。
brief.outcomeZh: 能表達有出處的內心傾向，分清工作身分及觀點。

listening.en: Although she managed the shop, Lena described herself as a teacher at heart, because she most enjoyed showing new assistants how to solve a problem rather than simply giving them the answer.
listening.zh: 雖管店，Lena 說自己內心是老師，因最享受教新助手怎解問題，而非只給答案。
listening.promptZh: 這自我描述指甚麼？

options.en: She enjoys helping assistants learn, not necessarily holding a formal teaching post.
options.zh: 她享受幫助手學，不必指有正式教職。

options.en: She has left the shop and now works only in a school.
options.zh: 她已離店，現只在學校工作。

options.en: She avoids explaining and gives assistants only finished answers.
options.zh: 她避解釋，只給助手完成答案。

options.en: She completed a formal teaching qualification before beginning to manage the shop.
options.zh: 她開始管店前已取得正式教學資格。

listening.explanationZh: 內心教師傾向由喜歡引導解題支持，不是改職業、只給答案或已有資格的證明。

reply.promptZh: Lena 為甚麼說自己內心像老師？
reply.promptEn: Why does Lena describe herself as someone who loves teaching?

options.en: She most enjoys showing new assistants how to solve a problem.
options.zh: 她最享受教新助手怎解問題。

options.en: She is a teacher at heart because helping others learn is what she enjoys most.
options.zh: 她內心是老師，因最享受幫別人學。

options.en: Guiding someone through a problem matters more to her than just supplying an answer.
options.zh: 引導人解問題對她比只供答案更重要。

options.en: Her favourite part of managing the shop is helping assistants understand what they are doing.
options.zh: 管店最喜歡部分，是幫助手懂所做的事。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以喜歡引導學習說內在傾向，不聲稱教學資格或已換職。

scene.promptZh: 角色是會計，但每晚都畫身邊人，自己說畫畫是最想長久保留的事，尚未決定轉職。哪句有適當範圍？

options.en: He describes himself as an artist at heart, while his current job remains accounting.
options.zh: 他說自己內心是藝術家，目前工作仍是會計。

options.en: The description means he now earns his income mainly from selling paintings.
options.zh: 描述表示他現在主要靠賣畫賺收入。

options.en: He has stopped drawing because accounting is his current job.
options.zh: 目前工作是會計，所以他已停畫。

scene.explanationZh: 有自述及持續畫支持內心興趣，不等於現靠賣畫或已停愛好。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 an artist at heart 推出？

options.en: The person has a deep interest or inclination towards art.
options.zh: 當事人對藝術有深興趣或傾向。

options.en: The person necessarily earns their living as a professional artist.
options.zh: 當事人必以專業藝術家工作謀生。

options.en: The statement may be a self-description rather than a formal job title.
options.zh: 說法可屬自我描述，而非正式職銜。

contrast.explanationZh: 內心傾向與職業收入不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想因 Lena 自認內心老師，就把店長職銜改成學校教師，但她仍在店管理。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Keep her shop role and quote what she values about teaching assistants, rather than invent a different job.
options.zh: 保留管店角色，引用她重視教助手甚麼，不編另一職業。

options.en: List schoolteacher as her current job without asking about any actual post.
options.zh: 不問實際職位，就列學校教師作現職。

options.en: Remove her interest in teaching from the profile because it is not her job title.
options.zh: 因教學不是職銜，就從人物介紹刪其興趣。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可保留實際工作及內心傾向，不編職業，也不因不是職銜便抹去興趣。

speaking.en: I am a storyteller at heart, although my daily work also involves organising the practical details.
speaking.zh: 我內心是說故事的人，雖日常工作也涉及安排實務細節。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清內心傾向與實際職責。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替朋友寫短介紹，他同意你說他內心好奇，因每到陌生地方都先問居民生活，亦會承認不知道；但他不想被寫成專家。用一至兩句英文依他意願作介紹，給一項行動支持，不推他懂所有地方。

examples.en: He is curious at heart, asking residents about daily life whenever he visits somewhere unfamiliar. He is happy to admit what he does not know and gives people time to explain their experience.
examples.zh: 他內心好奇，每到陌生地方便問居民日常；他樂於承認不懂，也讓人有時間解釋自己的經驗。

examples.en: At heart, he wants to understand how other people live rather than arrive with ready-made answers. On his visits, he listens to residents’ accounts and asks what he has not yet understood.
examples.zh: 他內心想理解別人怎生活，不是帶着現成答案到場；探訪時他聽居民敘述，也問還未懂之處。

glossary.en: admit what he does not know

writing.selfCheckZh: 以訪陌生地問居民及承認不懂支持好奇性情，尊重朋友同意範圍，不用專家或全知稱號。

takeaways.en: She was an explorer at heart, always asking what lay behind the familiar account of a place.
takeaways.zh: 她內心是探索者，總問地方熟悉敘述背後還有甚麼。

takeaways.en: He called himself a teacher at heart while explaining why he enjoyed helping the new volunteers learn.
takeaways.zh: 他解釋為何享受幫新義工學習時，說自己內心是老師。

brief.meaningEn: An area of activity or experience that someone does not yet know well.
brief.meaningZh: 某人尚未熟悉的活動或經驗領域。
brief.grammar: be/enter unfamiliar territory; something is unfamiliar territory for/to someone; no article is normally needed before this uncountable metaphor.
brief.register: Established territory-as-experience image. It describes limited familiarity, not inevitable fear, danger or permanent inability.
brief.boundaryZh: 不熟與不願學、無能力不同，需說哪部分新及可怎了解；同一任務可有熟悉與陌生部分。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能因一處新便否定所有已有經驗，也不應把承認不懂當已失敗。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出知識範圍，並提出具體求教或探索。

listening.en: Organising the photographs was familiar, but editing their sound commentary was unfamiliar territory for me; I asked to watch one short edit before trying a practice copy.
listening.zh: 整理照片很熟悉，但剪它們的聲音解說對我是不熟領域；我請先看一次短剪接，再試練習複本。
listening.promptZh: 陌生的是哪部分，先做甚麼？

options.en: Sound editing was new, so the speaker wanted a demonstration before a practice attempt.
options.zh: 剪聲音是新的，所以說話者想先看示範再練。

options.en: The speaker had never organised photographs and refused any practice.
options.zh: 說話者從未整理照片，拒任何練習。

options.en: The sound edit had already been completed independently before the request.
options.zh: 提出請求前，聲音剪接已獨立完成。

options.en: The only unfamiliar part was choosing which photograph to keep, not editing sound.
options.zh: 只有選留哪張照片陌生，不是剪聲音。

listening.explanationZh: 照片熟而聲音新，先看再練保留已有經驗，不是整項不會或已獨立完成。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你想先看一次聲音剪接？
reply.promptEn: Why would you like to watch a sound edit first?

options.en: I know the photograph work, but I have not learned the sound-editing part yet.
options.zh: 我懂照片工作，但尚未學聲音剪接。

options.en: Sound editing is unfamiliar territory for me, so a short demonstration would help me begin.
options.zh: 聲音剪接對我是不熟領域，所以短示範可幫開始。

options.en: I want to understand a new part before trying it on a practice copy.
options.zh: 我想先懂新部分，再試練習複本。

options.en: Watching one edit would give me a starting point for the part I do not yet know.
options.zh: 看一次剪接可給尚不懂部分的起點。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以新技能說示範需要，不否認照片工作經驗。

scene.promptZh: 你熟悉城市故事資料，首次寫太空幻想，想學如何建構虛構規則，沒有說真實科學資料可隨意編。哪句貼切？

options.en: Building a fictional world is unfamiliar territory for me, even though I know how to research a city story.
options.zh: 建構虛構世界對我是不熟領域，雖我懂研究城市故事。

options.en: I can use the city’s historical records to verify which invented rule governs this imaginary planet.
options.zh: 我可用城市歷史記錄，核實這虛構星球採哪項自創規則。

options.en: The new task is to collect more city records, not to decide how an invented world works.
options.zh: 新任務是收更多城市記錄，不是決定虛構世界怎運作。

scene.explanationZh: 已有研究能力仍可面對新創作框架；城市史料不能核實自創星球規則，新任務也不只是繼續收舊資料。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 unfamiliar territory 推出？

options.en: Someone lacks familiarity with a particular area.
options.zh: 某人不熟某範疇。

options.en: They are permanently incapable of learning about it.
options.zh: 他們永久無法學該領域。

options.en: They may have relevant skills from another area.
options.zh: 他們可能有另一領域相關技巧。

contrast.explanationZh: 不熟是目前經驗範圍，不是永久能力判決。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想因聲音剪接新，就把你原先照片整理也全收回；你可繼續照片並先看聲音示範。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Keep the work I know and support one first step in sound editing, rather than treat a new skill as no experience at all.
options.zh: 保留我懂的工作，支援聲音剪接第一步，不把新技能當全無經驗。

options.en: Remove both tasks and let me wait without a chance to see the unfamiliar step.
options.zh: 兩任務都移走，讓我等而無機會看陌生步驟。

options.en: Give me the finished sound file to approve without first showing how the edit works.
options.zh: 未示範剪接怎做，就給我完成聲音檔批准。

dialogue.explanationZh: 按範圍支援而非全排除或直接評未學技能。

speaking.en: This is unfamiliar territory for me, so I would like to identify the new part and ask one specific question before I begin.
speaking.zh: 這對我是不熟領域，所以想先指出新部分，開始前問一條具體問題。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再指明陌生範圍及求教。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你獲邀在小刊寫一段舞蹈觀後感，平常只評文字。你想接受探索，但向編輯坦白自己不熟舞蹈術語，提議先記動作帶來的感受，再請舞者核你對動作的描述，不假裝評技術等級。用一至兩句英文回覆。
writing.selfCheckZh: 坦白術語及技術評級限制，保留觀察感受及請核描述的貢獻，不把不熟變全拒或假專家。

examples.en: Dance criticism is unfamiliar territory for me, though I would like to explore it. Could I begin with what the movement made me notice, then ask a dancer to check my description rather than claim to rank the technique?
examples.zh: 舞評對我是不熟領域，但我想探索；可否先寫動作令我留意甚麼，再請舞者核描述，不自稱可評技術等級？

examples.en: I can describe my response to the performance, but technical dance language is unfamiliar territory. I would welcome help checking the movement descriptions before the piece goes into the magazine.
examples.zh: 我可描述演出帶來的反應，但舞蹈術語是不熟領域；刊物用稿前，我歡迎幫核動作描述。

takeaways.en: The new software was unfamiliar territory for the volunteers, so they began with a short guided task.
takeaways.zh: 新軟件對義工是不熟領域，所以先做短引導任務。

takeaways.en: She enjoyed entering unfamiliar territory in her writing while asking for help with the details she had not yet learned.
takeaways.zh: 她喜歡在寫作進不熟領域，同時在尚未學的細節求助。

brief.meaningEn: Extremely quickly, often with a sense of haste or intensity.
brief.meaningZh: 極快速地，常帶急促或強烈感。
brief.grammar: move/work/develop/change at breakneck speed; figurative intensifier, not a measured speed or a statement that an injury occurred.
brief.register: Emphatic fixed phrase. Depending on context the pace may be exciting, difficult to follow or in need of checking.
brief.boundaryZh: 快不自證好壞、正確或完成全部，亦不是字面受傷；需指出哪個過程快及實際影響。
brief.misconceptionZh: 速度與品質需分開看，不因用詞強烈便編事故或成功。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述急速過程並依具體影響提出回應。

listening.en: The rehearsal moved at breakneck speed after the new scenes arrived: we tried four transitions in twenty minutes, but the director marked two places to revisit rather than call the whole sequence finished.
listening.zh: 新場景到後，排練以極快速度進行；二十分鐘試四次轉場，但導演標兩處再看，沒稱整段已完。
listening.promptZh: 急速之中已做甚麼，仍需甚麼？

options.en: Four transitions were tried quickly, with two places still marked for another look.
options.zh: 快速試了四次轉場，兩處仍標待再看。

options.en: The director had approved every transition as ready for the public performance.
options.zh: 導演已批每次轉場可公開演。

options.en: The rehearsal stopped before any new transition could be attempted.
options.zh: 未試任何新轉場，排練便停。

options.en: Twenty minutes were spent discussing only one unchanged transition without trying it.
options.zh: 二十分鐘只談一個未變轉場，沒有試。

listening.explanationZh: 快的是試轉場，兩處仍待看，不是全批、未試或只談一處。

reply.promptZh: 新場景到後，排練怎進行？
reply.promptEn: How did the rehearsal proceed after the new scenes arrived?

options.en: We tried four transitions in twenty minutes and marked two points for another look.
options.zh: 二十分鐘試四轉場，標兩點再看。

options.en: It moved at breakneck speed, though two parts still needed revisiting.
options.zh: 它以極快速度進行，雖兩部分仍需再看。

options.en: The pace was very rapid, not a claim that the whole sequence was finished.
options.zh: 節奏很快，不是聲稱整段已完成。

options.en: Several transitions were tested in a short time, with follow-up still planned.
options.zh: 短時間試幾轉場，仍計劃跟進。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說急速試行及待看範圍，不把快當全完。

scene.promptZh: 故事開場一頁內連續介紹六個人物及三次地點轉換，讀者說跟不上；編輯建議加一段停下的對話，未決刪人物。哪句準確？

options.en: The opening moves at breakneck speed, so a pause may help readers follow it.
options.zh: 開場以極快速度推進，所以停一停可能幫讀者跟上。

options.en: The editor has already decided to remove all six characters from the story.
options.zh: 編輯已決刪故事六個人物。

options.en: The reader’s difficulty comes from a long scene in one place with only one speaker.
options.zh: 讀者困難來自同地點只有一人說話的長場景。

scene.explanationZh: 連介紹及換地點形成急促，所提是加停頓，未決刪人。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 at breakneck speed 推出？

options.en: The process is very fast.
options.zh: 過程很快。

options.en: The result has necessarily been checked and found correct.
options.zh: 結果必已核並確認正確。

options.en: Context determines whether the pace helps or hinders the task.
options.zh: 情境決定速度有助還是妨礙任務。

contrast.explanationZh: 快本身不證核對或正確。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說二十分鐘試了四轉場，就不用看導演標的兩處；你想用標記完成後續。哪個回應最好？

options.en: The pace was quick, but the marked points tell us what to review before calling the sequence ready.
options.zh: 節奏快，但標記告訴我們稱整段備妥前需看甚麼。

options.en: Repeat the whole sequence at an even faster pace and leave the two marked points undiscussed.
options.zh: 以更快速度重跑全段，不談兩標記。

options.en: Remove both marked transitions immediately without checking what the director wanted changed.
options.zh: 未查導演想改甚麼，就立即刪兩個標記轉場。

dialogue.explanationZh: 按標記處理，不以更快代回顧，也不未核就刪。

speaking.en: The lesson moved at breakneck speed, and I asked for a pause to understand how the examples connected.
speaking.zh: 課堂以極快速度進行，我請停一停理解示例怎相連。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把速度與理解需要分清。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你們現場布展時，入口及輪值安排每幾分鐘便改，幫手收到互相矛盾舊訊息。你想在群組說變動很快，提把已確認安排集中在一張有時間的更新表，由一人改；未確認仍標待定，不只叫大家看快些。用一至兩句英文提出。

examples.en: The arrangements are changing at breakneck speed, and helpers are receiving different versions. Could we keep one time-stamped update sheet, with one person entering confirmed changes and leaving unresolved points marked as pending?
examples.zh: 安排以極快速度變，幫手收到不同版本；可否用一張有時間標記的更新表，由一人填已確認改動，未解決仍標待定？

examples.en: We are moving at breakneck speed, so I suggest a single current summary rather than another stream of separate messages. Let one coordinator update the agreed arrangements while keeping unconfirmed changes clearly labelled.
examples.zh: 我們以極快速度推進，所以我提一份最新摘要，不再添一串獨立訊息；由一位統籌更新議定安排，未確認改動清楚標明。

glossary.zh: 一張有時間標記的更新表

writing.selfCheckZh: 以安排急變說極快，集中已確認版本並保待定，不把快變當已確定，也不把負擔推給幫手自行追訊息。

takeaways.en: The plans changed at breakneck speed during the final week, so the coordinator kept one current list for the team.
takeaways.zh: 最後一周計劃以極快速度改變，所以統籌為團隊保留一份最新清單。

takeaways.en: The story moves at breakneck speed until a quiet exchange gives the reader time to understand the choice.
takeaways.zh: 故事極快推進，直到一段安靜交流給讀者時間理解選擇。

titleZh: 感到被變化洪流推着走

brief.meaningEn: Feel carried forward by changing events or demands rather than directing one’s own response.
brief.meaningZh: 感到被變化事件或要求往前帶，而非自己掌握回應。
brief.grammar: feel/be swept along by a current; a current is a creative flow-of-events image, not evidence of literal water. Feeling carried need not prove complete absence of choice.
brief.register: Extended river metaphor. Name the events or pressures and distinguish felt lack of control from unavoidable force.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是字面水流，也不必有人惡意；需有連續變化及當事人反應，不因比喻就說完全無法選擇。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可承認壓力，同時提出暫停、問清或分優先等小幅主動。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體變化說明被推着走的感受，並表達想重掌的一步。

sources.sentence: Without guidance, new users may feel swept along by a current.

listening.en: As the workshop dates and roles kept changing, I felt swept along by a current, agreeing to each new arrangement before understanding what it replaced; I asked for one clear summary before replying again.
listening.zh: 工作坊日期及角色不停改時，我感到被洪流推着走，未懂新安排取代甚麼便逐一答應；再回覆前，我請求一份清楚總結。
listening.promptZh: 被推着走的感受連到甚麼？

options.en: Repeated changes led to quick agreement before the speaker understood the current arrangement.
options.zh: 反覆改動令說話者未懂目前安排就快速答應。

options.en: The speaker had already compared every change with a clear personal plan before agreeing.
options.zh: 答應前，說話者已按清楚個人計劃比每項改動。

options.en: Only one unchanged arrangement was sent, with no changes in dates or roles.
options.zh: 只寄一份未改安排，日期及角色都沒變。

options.en: The summary had already been provided and understood before the changes began.
options.zh: 改動開始前，總結已提供並被理解。

listening.explanationZh: 連改及未懂先答應支持感受，總結仍是所請下一步。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你想再回覆前先有一份總結？
reply.promptEn: Why do you want a summary before replying again?

options.en: The changing arrangements were hard to follow before I agreed to each one.
options.zh: 各項改動難跟，我卻逐一答應。

options.en: I felt swept along by a current and wanted to understand the current plan before another commitment.
options.zh: 我感到被洪流推着走，想再承諾前先懂目前計劃。

options.en: I needed to see what the new dates and roles had replaced.
options.zh: 我需看新日期及角色取代了甚麼。

options.en: A single summary would help me choose a response instead of reacting to each change separately.
options.zh: 一份總結可幫選回應，不再對每項改動分別反應。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以變化及先理解的需要解釋，不說已完全失去選擇。

scene.promptZh: 同學邀你跟風報一個熱門課，但你先比較兩課內容及時間，再選另一個更合自己問題的課，並說這次是自己想清楚選的。哪句最不符合？

options.en: I was swept along by a current of popularity, rather than comparing the courses and making my own choice.
options.zh: 我被熱門風潮推着走，沒有比較課程並自行選擇。

options.en: I considered the options and chose the course that better matched my own question.
options.zh: 我考慮選項，選較合自己問題的課。

options.en: My account describes a considered decision rather than simply following the popular option.
options.zh: 我的敘述是想清楚的決定，不是只跟熱門選項。

scene.explanationZh: 已比較並選另一合需要的課，與本人這次被潮流推走的描述不符；有外在邀請也可有主動選擇。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 felt swept along by a current 的比喻推出？

options.en: The person experienced events as carrying them forward.
options.zh: 當事人覺事件正帶自己往前。

options.en: There is no possible choice or response available to the person.
options.zh: 當事人沒有任何可選回應。

options.en: The context can show what changes created that feeling.
options.zh: 情境可顯示甚麼變化造成感受。

contrast.explanationZh: 感受不自證完全無自主，小步問清仍可有。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說既然你感到被帶着走，就只能繼續答應所有改動；你想先懂安排。哪個回應最好？

options.en: I can ask what the latest plan replaces and take time to decide, rather than answer each change immediately.
options.zh: 我可問最新計劃取代甚麼並留時間決定，不立即回每改動。

options.en: Agree to the next change first and ask for its meaning after the commitment is announced.
options.zh: 先答應下項改動，宣布承諾後才問意思。

options.en: Stop replying without telling the group which responsibilities I have already accepted.
options.zh: 不告小組已接哪些責任，就停止回覆。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可先問清並交代已接責任，不只能盲答或不清交接便消失。

speaking.en: I felt swept along by a current of changes, so I asked for a pause to understand what I had actually agreed to.
speaking.zh: 我感到被改動洪流推着走，所以請暫停，理解自己實際答應甚麼。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再連感受與可採取的小步。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你給合作故事提一段角色描寫，角色一整天只回應家人不同要求，晚上才發現沒做自己想寫的信。你想讓他承認被事情推着走的感受，接着用短便條向家人說明會先留半小時寫信，不把家人寫成故意害他。用一至兩句英文提議這段發展。
writing.selfCheckZh: 描寫連續要求及未寫信的感受，安排向家人交代小幅選擇，不編惡意或把被帶着走寫成永久無法主動。

examples.en: He feels swept along by a current of requests and notices that his letter is still unwritten. I would have him leave a note saying he will keep half an hour for it, rather than accuse the family of planning to stop him.
examples.zh: 他感到被要求洪流推着走，發現信仍未寫；我會讓他留便條說先留半小時寫，不指控家人計劃阻他。

examples.en: The day leaves him feeling swept along by a current, but the next scene can show a small choice. He tells the family he will write for half an hour before taking on another request.
examples.zh: 那天讓他感到被洪流推着走，但下幕可展示小選擇；他告家人會先寫半小時，再接另一要求。

takeaways.en: The newcomers felt swept along by a current until the mentor helped them identify one decision they could make themselves.
takeaways.zh: 導師幫新人找一項可自己決定的事前，他們感到被洪流推着走。

takeaways.en: I was swept along by a current of invitations and needed time to decide which ones I could genuinely accept.
takeaways.zh: 我被邀請洪流帶着走，需要時間決定哪些真能接受。

brief.meaningEn: With a manageable amount of trouble or inconvenience rather than excessive difficulty.
brief.meaningZh: 只有可應付的麻煩或不便，而非過多困難。
brief.grammar: do/change/arrange something without too much hassle; hassle is normally uncountable in this phrase; too much allows some minor trouble.
brief.register: Everyday informal collocation. It can describe someone’s particular experience without promising the same ease for everyone.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是完全無事做或沒有任何不便，需保留所述小阻礙及範圍；不把一人經驗當普遍保證。
brief.misconceptionZh: 有一點等候仍可說沒有太多麻煩，不能把程度詞抹掉。
brief.outcomeZh: 能平衡描述順利處理及少量實際不便。

sources.sentence: We changed trains without too much hassle.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 36, table 2, row 4; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: We changed the workshop room without too much hassle: one phone call and a short form settled it, though we had to wait until the next morning for the key.
listening.zh: 我們沒有太多麻煩就換了工作坊房間；一通電話及短表格便辦妥，不過需等翌早才拿鑰匙。
listening.promptZh: 整體順利與小不便是甚麼？

options.en: The change needed a call and short form, with a wait for the key until morning.
options.zh: 更改需電話及短表，並等翌早拿鑰匙。

options.en: The room was changed without any call, form or waiting at all.
options.zh: 換房完全不需電話、表或等候。

options.en: The key was available immediately before any request was made.
options.zh: 未提出要求前，鑰匙已立即可拿。

options.en: The change could not be arranged and the workshop had to be cancelled.
options.zh: 無法安排換房，工作坊需取消。

listening.explanationZh: 少量程序及等鑰匙仍可不太麻煩，不是零程序或未辦成。

reply.promptEn: Was changing the workshop room troublesome?

options.en: It was manageable: a call and a short form, with the key available the next morning.
options.zh: 可應付；電話加短表，翌早有鑰匙。

options.en: We did it without too much hassle, though we waited until morning for the key.
options.zh: 沒有太多麻煩便做了，雖等早上拿鑰匙。

options.en: The process was fairly straightforward rather than completely free of waiting.
options.zh: 流程頗直接，不是完全不用等。

options.en: There were only a few steps, and the remaining wait was for the key.

scene.promptZh: 你搬小房間，紙箱早已分類，朋友幫兩次搬上樓，電梯仍等了十分鐘；你覺可應付。哪句符合？

options.en: We moved the boxes without too much hassle, despite a short wait for the lift.
options.zh: 雖短等電梯，我們沒太多麻煩便搬好箱。

options.en: We moved everything without needing a friend, a lift or any waiting.
options.zh: 我們不需朋友、電梯或等候便搬好全部。

options.en: The wait prevented the boxes from being moved upstairs at all.
options.zh: 等候令箱子完全無法搬上樓。

scene.explanationZh: 已分類及協助使可應付，短等仍存在，不是零幫助或完全搬不到。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 without too much hassle 推出？

options.en: The inconvenience was not excessive in that experience.
options.zh: 那次經驗不便不算過多。

options.en: There was absolutely no effort, waiting or minor problem.
options.zh: 絕對沒有努力、等候或小問題。

options.en: Some manageable steps may still have been involved.
options.zh: 仍可能涉及一些可應付步驟。

contrast.explanationZh: too much限制過量，不把所有麻煩都否定。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想在活動日記刪等鑰匙，因你說沒太多麻煩；等候確有發生。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Keep the short wait in the account; the phrase describes the trouble as manageable, not absent.
options.zh: 保留短等候；詞組說麻煩可應付，不是不存在。

options.en: Leave out the key stage and say the room was ready immediately after the call.
options.zh: 刪拿鑰匙階段，說打電話後房間立即備好。

options.en: Describe the whole change as unsuccessful because the key was not available at once.
options.zh: 因鑰匙不是立即有，就把整個更改寫成失敗。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可順利且需短等，不抹事實或把小等候等同失敗。

speaking.en: We arranged it without too much hassle, although there were a few simple steps and a short wait.
speaking.zh: 雖有幾項簡單步驟及短等候，我們沒太多麻煩便安排好。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再保留程度詞及實際小不便。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你向家人說第一次把舊照片分裝給幾位親人，先用名字貼紙及一份清單，寄出前有一個錯盒需重放，但最後順利。你想寫兩句平實近況，承認小修正又不說整次糟透，不提供寄送價格建議。用一至兩句英文表達。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以標籤清單及已完成分裝說可應付，也承認寄前重裝一盒，不把小修正抹去或誇成全失敗。

examples.en: I sorted the photographs for the family without too much hassle, using name labels and a simple list. One box needed repacking before I sent it, but the overall process was manageable.
examples.zh: 我用姓名標籤及簡單清單，沒太多麻煩便分好家族照片；寄出前一盒需重裝，但整個流程可應付。

examples.en: The labels helped me prepare the different sets without too much hassle. I corrected one mix-up before sending them, rather than pretend there were no small changes to make.
examples.zh: 標籤幫我沒太多麻煩備好不同照片組；寄前改了一項混淆，不假裝全沒小改動。

takeaways.en: The new member joined the group without too much hassle after a short introduction and one simple form.
takeaways.zh: 短介紹及一張簡單表後，新成員沒太多麻煩便加入。

takeaways.en: We found the borrowed book without too much hassle, though we checked two shelves before locating it.
takeaways.zh: 雖查兩個書架才找到，我們仍沒太多麻煩便找回借書。

titleZh: 書面看來理想，實際仍需了解

brief.meaningEn: Appear favourable, effective or secure in a written description or plan, while practical experience may still differ or need checking.
brief.meaningZh: 在書面描述或計劃中看來理想、有效或穩妥，但實際體驗可能不同，仍需要了解。
brief.grammar: look/looks/looked impressive, good, secure or more secure on paper; the adjective names the quality suggested by the description. More secure introduces a comparison, which the surrounding context should identify. The plan/offer frame differs from describing a person’s credentials as brilliant on paper, though both use the related on-paper contrast.
brief.register: Conventional on-paper contrast. It often introduces a reservation, but the phrase alone does not prove the plan will fail or that the written features are false.
brief.boundaryZh: 書面上看來理想或穩妥，可以與實際限制並存；需要說明哪項條件仍待了解，不能把這個對比說成所有書面資料都不可信。
brief.misconceptionZh: 尚未試過，不等於已失敗；清單豐富或條款看來穩妥，也不等於已證明適合實際需要。
brief.outcomeZh: 能區分書面呈現的優點或穩妥程度、實際體驗，以及仍需要核對的事項。

listening.en: The rehearsal plan looked impressive on paper, with time for every scene and a discussion at the end, but the forty-five-minute room booking left no space for moving the set between scenes.
listening.zh: 排練計劃書面看來出色，有每幕及最後討論的時間，但四十五分鐘房間預約沒留幕間移景時間。
listening.promptZh: 書面吸引力與實際落差是甚麼？

options.en: The plan covered scenes and discussion but omitted the time needed to move the set.
options.zh: 計劃包括場景及討論，卻漏移景所需時間。

options.en: The plan already included enough time for set moves inside the booking.
options.zh: 計劃已在預約內留足移景時間。

options.en: The written plan contained no scenes and only an equipment list.
options.zh: 書面計劃沒場景，只有器材清單。

options.en: The room booking had already been extended before the timing issue was raised.
options.zh: 提出時間問題前，房間預約已延長。

listening.explanationZh: 場景表豐富但漏轉場實務時間，沒有說已補或已延期。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你說排練計劃寫來好，仍有問題？
reply.promptEn: Why do you say the rehearsal plan looks strong but still has a problem?

options.en: The scene schedule leaves out the time needed to move the set.
options.zh: 場景表漏移景所需時間。

options.en: It looked impressive on paper, but the booking did not allow for changes between scenes.
options.zh: 它書面看來出色，但預約沒容幕間轉換。

options.en: The written coverage is broad, while the actual room time is limited.
options.zh: 書面涵蓋廣，實際房間時間卻有限。

options.en: Including every scene in a list does not create the extra minutes the set moves require.
options.zh: 清單列每幕，不會多出移景所需分鐘。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都給具體時間落差，不只說所有計劃沒用。

scene.promptZh: 工作坊介紹列很多活動，看來吸引，但尚未問房間可否同時容分組及材料桌；你想保留評價與未知。哪句準確？

options.en: The programme looks good on paper, but we still need to check how the room can support the activities.
options.zh: 活動書面看來好，但仍需查房間怎支援各活動。

options.en: The room has already been tested and cannot support any part of the programme.
options.zh: 房間已測，不能支援活動任何部分。

options.en: The long activity list is itself evidence that the room arrangement has been settled.
options.zh: 長活動清單本身是房間安排已定的證據。

scene.explanationZh: 清單吸引與場地待查不同，未試不等於已不可用，也不證安排已定。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 looks impressive on paper 推出？

options.en: The written description appears attractive.
options.zh: 書面描述看來吸引。

options.en: Actual use is already known to be either perfect or a failure.
options.zh: 已知實際使用不是完美就是失敗。

options.en: Context may reveal practical conditions not captured in the description.
options.zh: 情境可顯實際條件未在描述中涵蓋。

contrast.explanationZh: 看來好不自定實際結果，需看後續資料。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想因表上列齊場景，就不算移景時間；但房間只四十五分鐘。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Add the set moves to the timing trial and adjust the scope before treating the plan as workable.
options.zh: 把移景納計時試行，稱計劃可行前先調範圍。

options.en: Keep the list unchanged and begin the discussion before checking whether the set can be moved in time.
options.zh: 保持清單不變，未查移景來得及便開始討論。

options.en: Shorten the final discussion to make room for the listed scenes before checking how long the set moves take.
options.zh: 未核移景需時，先縮最後討論來容納清單各幕。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先把移景納計時再調範圍，不能漏計它，也不應未量實際時間便先刪討論。

speaking.en: The proposal looks impressive on paper, but I want to test the practical conditions before saying it meets our needs.
speaking.zh: 提案書面看來出色，但稱它合需要前，我想測實際條件。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清書面吸引力與實際合用。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你改一段小說日記，角色原被住所介紹的安靜書角及大窗吸引，到了才發現窗正對每天排練的廣場。你想保留她最初為何期待，又寫實際聲音如何改感受，不說廣告所有內容都假，也不寫租屋建議。用一至兩句英文寫日記語氣。
writing.selfCheckZh: 保留書角大窗的最初期待及窗確實存在，用實際聲音改感受，不把一項未涵蓋等同全部造假。

examples.en: The room looked impressive on paper, with a reading corner and a large window, so I arrived expecting quiet. Then the rehearsal in the square reached the window, and the space felt different from what I had imagined.
examples.zh: 房間書面看來出色，有書角及大窗，所以我到時期待安靜；廣場排練聲傳進窗，空間感受便跟想像不同。

examples.en: It looked good on paper, and the window really was as large as described. What the description did not show was how the daily rehearsal outside would fill the reading corner with sound.
examples.zh: 它書面看來好，窗確實如描述般大；描述沒顯示的是外面每天排練怎讓書角充滿聲音。

takeaways.en: The offer looked impressive on paper, but the timetable left her little time for the work she most wanted to do.
takeaways.zh: 提議書面看來出色，但時間表讓她少有時間做最想做的工作。

takeaways.en: Our new layout looks good on paper, so we are asking first-time visitors to try it before making a wider claim.
takeaways.zh: 新版面書面看來好，所以我們先請首次訪客試，再作較廣聲稱。

titleZh: 最初的新鮮吸引力很快消退

brief.meaningEn: The initial excitement or attraction fades after someone becomes familiar with the experience or its difficulties.
brief.meaningZh: 熟習經驗或遇上其難處後，最初興奮或吸引力消退。
brief.grammar: the shine soon wears off; the shine wore/has worn off; the shine can wear off expresses possibility, with soon/quickly giving timing.
brief.register: Established shine-as-attraction metaphor. Losing novelty does not necessarily remove all lasting value or prove an initial description was false.
brief.boundaryZh: 吸引力減不等於完全沒用、所有人同感或事情已失敗；需有初期與後來感受的對比。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可欣賞仍有的作用，同時承認新鮮感退；不要把變化當物件外觀必壞。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述初期熱情及之後變化，分清感受與客觀功能。
